text:
anand: kicked off a 2h replaybench against main with the new hint-selector + adaptive-batcher. goal was apples-to-apples vs last stable. quick heads-up: we observed a regression on cold-start p95, particularly on dedicated pools (details below).

kelsey: ugh, how big is the regression?

anand: about 2.8x p95 for first-token latency on 8k sequence workloads; steady-state tps looks fine. it's mainly in the scale-up path + kernel selection delay.

ryan: can you paste the flame/profile? curious if kernel compile or kernel probe is the culprit.

anand: pasted the short profile from the 1st cold start run: ```
# top spans (wall ms)
kernel_probe: 470ms
kv_warmup_wait: 120ms
batcher_init: 95ms
runtime_select_kernel: 65ms
serve_request: 30ms
```
looks like kernel_probe dominates.

maria: FYI the hint-selector change added an extra verification step for mixed-precision safety (to avoid prior quantization artifacts). that check is async normally but we made it sync for correctness in the first rollout. could explain the probe + blocking.

anand: agree, I can repro by toggling the verification flag. when off, cold-start p95 drops back to ~1.1x baseline.

sara: any impact on batch shape heuristics? i.e., does the adaptive-batcher wait longer because of the probe and thus change observed batch sizes?

anand: yes — we see more single-request batches during the first 30s of scaleup. aggregate batch size median drops from 6 -> 2 in that window.

mike: KV cache metrics from the same runs: miss_rate spikes from 8% -> 22% during cold path. probably because the runtime is delaying cache priming until kernel selection completes.

replay-bot: replaybench logs uploaded: https://internal.redwood/replays/1943210000/run-42.tar.gz : includes raw traces + perf counters.

ryan: two action items: (1) revert the sync verification to async-first then background-validate, (2) add a timeout fallback on kernel_probe so we pick a safe default kernel after X ms and continue warming.

maria: +1. also propose we add an apples-to-apples synthetic test that runs the exact same model variant with and without the verification patch but keeps traffic mix identical. run it against dedicated pools and hosted to compare.

anand: prepping a targeted run now. also instrumenting a metric "kernel_probe_block_ms" and a sampling log that records chosen kernel id vs fallback.

sara: can autoscale-bot show whether burst credits were used by the dedicated pool during the incident run? i want to know if the burst bank masked upstream throttling.

autoscale-bot: pool "dedicated-pool-7" events during run-42: scale_up_start=1943210025, capacity_added=4 gpus, burst_credit_consumed=2.3, final_capacity=8, scale_up_complete=1943210062.

mike: so burst credits were used but still had cold p95 spikes. suggests the issue is local startup latency not global capacity.

kelsey: let's keep the rollback ready and run the async validation experiment A/B in staging then promote if stable. timeline?

anand: I can run the A/B within 2 hours. baseline replay vs patch replay + synthetic apples-to-apples for a 30m window each. will post results.

ryan: also add a microbench for kernel selection that runs many small coldstarts in a loop and records kernel probe time distribution. that will isolate the probe cost without KV/batching noise.

anand: noted. will upload a 30-run microbench and the 2 A/B runs to the replay link above.

maria: thanks — let's try not to ship the sync verification as default until we have async-safety + fallback. :thumbsup:

anand: +1. will follow up with PR to flip flag and a short doc on the fallback heuristic.

mike: one more note: if we keep the probe but memoize probe results across model variants (where safe), we can amortize cost. add that to the long-term follow-ups.

anand: added to follow-ups. I'll ping when uploads are done.
